title: graphics.bitmap.decode request
description: Decode a planar region into one palette index per pixel. Deliberately stops at indices: which colors they mean, which planes a viewer has switched off, and what a transparent pixel looks like are presentation choices that belong to whatever displays the result.

offset.description: Byte offset of the planar data within the source.

shape.description: What the region decodes to. `bitmap` is one image; `glyph_sheet` tiles `glyph_count` images into a contact sheet; `bob` is one blitter object whose mask says which pixels are opaque.

width.description: Pixel width of one image; for `glyph_sheet`, of one glyph.

height.description: Pixel height of one image; for `glyph_sheet`, of one glyph.

planes.description: Bitplanes. The blitter addresses at most eight, and a palette index is one byte.

plane_order.description: `contiguous` stores every row of one plane before the next; `interleaved` stores all planes of each row together; `byte_interleaved`, `word_interleaved`, and `longword_interleaved` store all planes of each 8-, 16-, or 32-pixel chunk together, which are storage layouts code scatters into bitplanes at load time rather than ones the chipset displays.

glyph_count.description: `glyph_sheet` only: how many glyphs to decode.

glyph_columns.description: `glyph_sheet` only: glyphs per row of the contact sheet.

glyph_gap.description: `glyph_sheet` only: separator pixels between tiled glyphs.

maximum_output_pixels.description: Refuse a decode whose output would exceed this many pixels. Checked from the declared geometry before anything is read, because a planar decode's cost is its output rather than its input.
